site.name: Acme Console
site.notes:
Acme Console is where teams manage their Acme projects, teammates and subscription.

- Everything about the account (settings, plan, payment, security) is under the round "A" button at the top right.
- Billing details are changed with "Update payment method" on the Plan and billing page. We don't store full card numbers.
- API keys are on the Security tab of Settings.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
# API keys

An API key lets the Acme command line tool and your own scripts act for your workspace without anyone signing in. You need one to deploy.

API keys are on the Security tab of Settings. To create one:

1. Press the round "A" button at the top right and choose Settings.
2. Press the Security tab.
3. In the API keys section, press Create API key, below the list of keys.

The page shows "API key created." and the key is added to the list as "New key", with when it was created. The list never shows a key's secret value.

The secret is sent once, to the workspace owner's email address, as a link that can be opened one time within 24 hours. After that it cannot be read again by anyone, including Acme support. Keep it somewhere safe, such as a password manager. If you lose it, create another key and update your tools.

A key belongs to the workspace, not to a person or a project. It works for every project in both regions, and it keeps working if the person who was using it leaves the workspace. Keys do not expire, and they are not affected by the two-factor authentication requirement.

A key cannot be switched off from Acme Console. If a key may have been seen by someone outside your team, the owner should write to support and we switch it off, normally within one business day. Create the replacement key first, so that your deploys are not interrupted.

docs.title: Contacting support
docs.text:
# Contacting support

You can reach Acme support by email at support@acme.example. A person reads every message.

Support is open Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00 UTC, and is closed on 25 December and 1 January. We reply within one business day. Workspaces on the Business plan get a first reply within 4 working hours.

So that we can help in our first reply, tell us your workspace name, as it appears in Workspace name on the General tab of Settings. Add the project involved, if there is one, what you were trying to do, what happened instead, and when it happened.

Some requests are only accepted from the workspace owner's email address, because they change who or what can reach the workspace or how it is paid for. These are: switching off an API key, resetting a teammate's two-factor authentication, paying with a different card, and anything about refunds or unpaid invoices. If a member writes about one of these, we ask them to have the owner contact us.

Support will never ask for your password, an API key's secret value, a two-factor code or a full card number. If a message asks for any of these, do not answer it. Forward it to us instead.

There are things support cannot do. We cannot read an API key's secret value, and we cannot change a project's region or its name.

docs.title: Deploys
docs.text:
# Deploys

A deploy puts a new version of a project live. Deploys are started from your own computer or build system with the Acme command line tool, using one of the workspace's API keys. Acme Console shows the result; it has no button for starting a deploy.

On the Overview page, the Latest deploy card names the project that was deployed most recently and says how long ago it went live, for example "storefront-api went live 2 hours ago". The card covers every project in the workspace and counts successful deploys only. Its View projects link opens the Projects page.

A deploy usually takes about 2 minutes. The version that is already live keeps answering requests until the new one is ready, so there is no gap in service.

If a deploy fails, nothing changes: the previous version stays live. The command line tool prints the reason.

Each project runs one deploy at a time. A second deploy to the same project waits until the first has finished.

The workspace owner gets an email for every deploy, successful or failed, giving the project, the result and the time. The time is written in the workspace time zone.

Any teammate who has been given an API key can deploy to any project in the workspace. Deploys do not count as requests, so you can still deploy after the workspace has reached its request limit for the month.

There is no separate way to undo a deploy. To go back to an earlier version, deploy that version again.

docs.title: Getting around Acme Console
docs.text:
# Getting around Acme Console

Acme Console is where teams manage their Acme projects, teammates and subscription.

Every page has the same bar at the top. On the left is the name Acme Console, which takes you to the Overview page. Next to it are three links: Overview, Projects and Team. At the top right is a round "A" button.

Overview is the first page you see. It says how many projects and teammates the workspace has, and it has two cards: Usage this month and Latest deploy.

Projects lists the workspace's projects and is where you create new ones. Team lists the people who can access the workspace and is where you invite more.

Everything about the account (settings, plan, payment, security) is under the round "A" button at the top right. Press it to open a menu with three choices: Settings, Plan and billing, and Sign out. Press the button again to close the menu.

Settings has three tabs. General holds the workspace name and time zone. Plan and billing holds your plan, payment method and invoices; it is the same page that Plan and billing in the menu opens. Security holds the two-factor authentication requirement and API keys.

Sign out ends your session in the browser you are using. Other browsers where you are signed in are not affected. If you do not sign out, you stay signed in on that browser for 30 days, and then you are asked to sign in again.

Acme Console works in the current versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge. Some changes can only be made by the workspace owner; the article Roles and removing people says which.

docs.title: Inviting teammates
docs.text:
# Inviting teammates

Anyone in a workspace can invite a new teammate. All you need is the person's email address.

1. Press Team in the bar at the top of the page.
2. Below the list of people, type the person's address in the Email address field.
3. Press Send invite.

The page shows "Invite sent." and the field is emptied, ready for the next address.

The person gets an email with a link that works for 7 days. They must accept with the same email address the invite was sent to. When they accept, they join the workspace as a member and their name appears in the list on the Team page. Until then they are not listed, and they do not count towards the number of people your plan allows.

If the link has run out, or the email never arrived, send the invite again: type the same address and press Send invite. The person gets a new link that works for another 7 days, and the earlier link stops working. You can re-send as many times as you need.

If the workspace already has as many people as its plan allows, the person cannot accept until a place is free or the workspace moves to a larger plan. The number of people each plan allows is in the article Usage and limits.

Only the workspace owner can remove people. The article Roles and removing people explains what members and the owner can each do.

docs.title: Payment method and invoices
docs.text:
# Payment method and invoices

Billing details are on the Plan and billing page. Press the round "A" button at the top right and choose Plan and billing.

The Payment method section shows the type of card and its last four digits, for example "Visa ending in 4242". We don't store full card numbers; our payment provider holds them.

Billing details are changed with Update payment method. Only the workspace owner can do this.

1. Press Update payment method.
2. In the dialog, fill in Name on card and Billing postcode. Both are required.
3. Press Save payment method. Press Cancel to leave things as they were.

The page shows "Payment method updated." The new details are used from the next charge. If an earlier charge failed, we try it again within an hour of you saving.

The dialog does not ask for a card number. To pay with a different card, the owner writes to support and we send a secure form from our payment provider, which works once and for 24 hours. A workspace has one payment method at a time. We accept Visa, Mastercard and American Express.

The Invoices section is below. Invoices are emailed on the 1st of each month, to the workspace owner's email address, and each one covers the month that is starting. Press Download latest invoice to get the most recent one. Earlier invoices are not listed on the page. They are in the monthly emails, and support can send a copy of any invoice from the last 12 months.

An invoice carries the workspace name, the name on the card and the billing postcode as they were on the day it was issued.

docs.title: Plans and billing
docs.text:
# Plans and billing

Your plan is on the Plan and billing page. Press the round "A" button at the top right and choose Plan and billing, or press the Plan and billing tab in Settings. The Current plan section names the plan you are on and what it costs a month.

There are three plans: Starter, Team and Business. Starter is free. Team is $49 a month. Business is $199 a month. Each price is for the whole workspace, however many people are in it, and does not include tax. What each plan includes is listed in the article Usage and limits.

Only the workspace owner can change the plan, with the Change plan button in the Current plan section.

Moving to a larger plan takes effect straight away. The difference for the days left in the month is added to your next invoice. Moving to a smaller plan takes effect on the 1st of the next month, and you keep the larger plan until then. To stop paying, move to Starter.

Paid plans are charged in advance, on the 1st of each month, to the payment method shown on the Plan and billing page.

The first payment on a paid plan is refunded in full if the owner asks within 14 days of the charge. After that, payments are not refunded, including for part of a month. To ask for a refund, the owner writes to support.

If the charge on the 1st fails, the owner is emailed and the invoice must be paid within 10 days, by the 11th of the month. If it is still unpaid on the 11th, deploys are paused and requests to your projects are refused until it is paid.

docs.title: Projects and regions
docs.text:
# Projects and regions

A project is one app or service that you run on Acme. Each project has its own deploys and its own web address. The Projects page lists every project in the workspace. Open it with Projects in the bar at the top, or with View projects on the Overview page.

To create a project:

1. On the Projects page, press New project, above the list.
2. In the New project dialog, type a name in Project name. A name is required.
3. Choose a Region: US East or EU West.
4. Press Create project. Press Cancel to close the dialog without creating anything.

The new project is added to the end of the list. It is empty until its first deploy.

Any teammate can create a project. The name becomes part of the project's web address, so it cannot be changed afterwards. We suggest lowercase letters and hyphens, as in storefront-api.

The region is where the project runs and where its data is kept. US East is in Virginia and EU West is in Ireland. Pick the one nearest to the people who use your app. US East is selected unless you choose EU West.

A region cannot be changed after a project is created. To run in the other region, create a second project there and deploy to it. The first project keeps running as before.

How many projects a workspace can have depends on its plan. The numbers are in the article Usage and limits.

docs.title: Roles and removing people
docs.text:
# Roles and removing people

The Team page lists the people who can access the workspace. Each of them has one of two roles: owner or member.

The owner is the person who created the workspace. A workspace has exactly one owner, and the list on the Team page shows "(owner)" after their name. Everyone else is a member, and anyone who accepts an invite joins as a member.

Members can create projects, deploy to any project in the workspace, invite teammates and see the workspace's usage on the Overview page.

Some things are for the owner only. Only the owner can remove people, change the plan, update the payment method, change the workspace name and time zone, turn the two-factor authentication requirement on or off, and create API keys.

Only the workspace owner can remove people. To remove someone, go to Team and press Remove next to their name.

The person loses access straight away and is signed out of Acme Console within a minute. Projects they created, and everything they deployed, stay in the workspace and keep running. Their place on the plan is free at once, so you can invite someone else.

The owner cannot be removed. A member cannot remove another member, and cannot remove themselves; they need to ask the owner.

Someone who has been removed can be invited again later. They need a new invite, and they come back as a member.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
# Two-factor authentication

With two-factor authentication, signing in takes a password and a 6-digit code from an authenticator app. The workspace owner can require it for everyone in the workspace.

To turn the requirement on:

1. Press the round "A" button at the top right and choose Settings.
2. Press the Security tab.
3. Tick Require two-factor authentication, at the top of the tab.

There is nothing to save. The change applies as soon as you tick the box, and the page shows "Two-factor authentication is now required."

Every teammate, the owner included, is then asked to set up two-factor authentication at their next sign-in. Nobody is signed out when you tick the box. People who are already signed in carry on until their session ends, which is at most 30 days later. Anyone who joins the workspace afterwards sets it up the first time they sign in.

Any authenticator app that produces 6-digit codes will work. Codes by text message are not supported. During setup each person is given 10 backup codes, and each backup code works once.

If someone loses the device that holds their authenticator app, they can sign in with a backup code. If they have no backup codes left, the owner can write to support to have that person's two-factor setup reset.

To stop requiring it, untick the box. The page shows "Two-factor authentication is no longer required." and teammates are no longer asked for a code, starting with their next sign-in.

docs.title: Usage and limits
docs.text:
# Usage and limits

Your usage for the current month is on the Overview page, in the Usage this month card. It reads, for example, "12,480 requests of 50,000 included." To get there, press Overview in the bar at the top of any page.

A request is one call received by any of your deployed projects. All the projects in a workspace share one total. A request counts whether your project answers it successfully or with an error. Deploys, and anything you do in Acme Console, do not count.

The count is brought up to date about every 10 minutes. It resets to zero on the 1st of each month, at midnight UTC. Requests you did not use are not carried over to the next month.

Each plan includes a number of requests a month, and sets how many projects and people a workspace can have. Starter includes 5,000 requests, 1 project and 2 people. Team includes 50,000 requests, 10 projects and 10 people. Business includes 500,000 requests, 50 projects and 50 people. The owner counts as one of the people.

When a workspace has used all its included requests, further requests are refused with a 429 response until the count resets or the workspace moves to a larger plan. Your projects and settings stay as they are.

The workspace owner gets an email when usage reaches 80% of the included requests, and another at 100%.

Moving to a larger plan raises the limit straight away. Requests already used that month still count. Changing plan is covered in the article Plans and billing.

docs.title: Workspace name and time zone
docs.text:
# Workspace name and time zone

The workspace name and time zone are on the General tab of Settings. Only the workspace owner can change them.

1. Press the round "A" button at the top right and choose Settings. Settings opens on the General tab.
2. Type a new name in Workspace name, or pick a zone from the Time zone list: UTC, Eastern or Pacific.
3. Press Save changes.

The page shows "Settings saved." Nothing changes until you press Save changes.

The workspace name is what teammates see in invite emails and what is printed at the top of invoices. Renaming the workspace does not affect your projects, their web addresses, your API keys or your teammates. The new name is used from the moment you save. Invoices that were already issued keep the old name.

The time zone changes the times shown on deploys and invoices: the time in each deploy email, and the dates on each invoice. There is one time zone for the whole workspace, so every teammate sees the same times. A new workspace starts on UTC. Eastern and Pacific follow daylight saving time automatically.

The time zone only changes how times are written. It does not move when things happen: usage still resets, and invoices are still issued, at midnight UTC on the 1st of each month.

The Latest deploy card on the Overview page says how long ago a deploy went live, such as "2 hours ago", so it reads the same in every time zone.

cases.question: how long is an invite good for before it lapses

expect.reference: The link in the invite email works for 7 days. If it runs out, sending the invite again gives the person a new link.

cases.question: When I press Send invite, does the person show up in the list above right away?

expect.reference: No, Send invite only emails the person a link. They join as a member and appear in the list on the Team page when they accept.

cases.question: do invites nobody has accepted yet use up one of our seats

expect.reference: No. A person who has not accepted yet is not listed and does not count towards the number of people the plan allows.

cases.question: What does (owner) after a name in this list mean? Can a workspace have two?

expect.reference: It marks the workspace's owner, the person who created it. There is exactly one owner per workspace, and everyone else is a member.

cases.question: One of our developers is leaving and will be taken off the team on Friday. She set up two of the projects. Do those disappear when she goes?

expect.reference: No. The projects that person created stay in the workspace and keep running, along with everything they deployed.

cases.question: can someone who was removd from the workspace be let back in later?

expect.reference: Yes, a removed person can be invited again. It takes a new invite, and they rejoin as a member.

cases.question: What counts as a "project" in here? One app, or a bundle of them?

expect.reference: One app or service that you run on Acme, not a group of them. Every project gets its own deploys and its own web address.

cases.question: what does New project want from me, just a name?

expect.reference: No, it asks for two things. New project opens a dialog with Project name, which is required, and Region, either US East or EU West.

cases.question: US East vs EU West: where are those physically?

expect.reference: US East runs in Virginia and EU West in Ireland. A project's region is where it runs and where its data is kept.

cases.question: What exactly is the Latest deploy box telling me? Is there one per project?

expect.reference: No, there is one card for the whole workspace: it names whichever project was deployed most recently and says how long ago it went live. Only successful deploys count.

cases.question: roughly how long does a deploy take and is the app offline while it runs

expect.reference: About 2 minutes, usually. The app is not down meanwhile: the version already live keeps answering requests until the new one is ready.

cases.question: What happens if two of us deploy to the same project at once?

expect.reference: A project runs only one deploy at a time, so the second one waits until the first has finished.

cases.question: After Create API key, where does the secret part turn up? The list only seems to show names.

expect.reference: Not in the list, which never shows a secret. It goes once to the workspace owner's email address, as a link that can be opened a single time within 24 hours.

cases.question: api keys - do they expire

expect.reference: No. API keys do not expire.

cases.question: does an api key belong to whoever set it up, or what

expect.reference: No, the key is the workspace's, not any one person's or project's. It keeps working after the person who was using it leaves the workspace.

cases.question: If I tick Require two-factor authentication, will everyone get kicked out and have to log in again?

expect.reference: No, ticking the box signs nobody out. Everyone, the owner included, is asked to set it up the next time they sign in, and anyone already signed in carries on until their session ends, at most 30 days later.

cases.question: can people get their two factor codes by sms insted of an app

expect.reference: No, codes are not sent by text message. They come from an authenticator app, and any app that produces 6-digit codes will do.

cases.question: What are the recovery codes you get when setting up two-factor for, and how many are there?

expect.reference: They are backup codes for signing in when someone has lost the device that holds their authenticator app. Each person gets 10 of them during setup, and each works once.

cases.question: is Time zone here only for what I see or does it change it for the whole team

expect.reference: It applies to the whole workspace: there is a single time zone, and every teammate sees the same times.

cases.question: If we rename the workspace, do our project URLs or API keys change?

expect.reference: No. A new workspace name leaves projects, their web addresses and API keys as they are, and teammates are not affected either.

cases.question: Does the Eastern time zone setting keep up with daylight savings by itself, or do we have to switch it twice a year?

expect.reference: It adjusts by itself: the Eastern and Pacific settings both follow daylight saving time automatically.

cases.question: How often does the number under Usage this month refresh? It looks like it lags behind what we're actually sending.

expect.reference: About every 10 minutes, which is how often the count is brought up to date. Requests received since the last update do not show yet.

cases.question: what counts as a reqest exactly, do ones that return an error count too

expect.reference: Anything received by one of your deployed projects is a request, and it counts whether the project answers successfully or with an error. Deploys and what you do in Acme Console are not counted.

cases.question: Does anybody get a heads-up before the monthly request allowance runs out?

expect.reference: Yes, the workspace owner is emailed twice: once when usage reaches 80% of the included requests and again at 100%.

cases.question: if we use Change plan to drop to a smaller one, does that kick in immediately

expect.reference: No. A move to a smaller plan takes effect on the 1st of the next month, and the workspace keeps the larger plan until then.

cases.question: can any of us switch the workspace to a bigger plan, or does it have to be one particular person

expect.reference: Only the workspace owner can change the plan. A member cannot.

cases.question: are the paid plans charged ahead of time or after the month is over

expect.reference: In advance: the charge for a paid plan is taken on the 1st of each month, from the payment method shown on the Plan and billing page.

cases.question: Does Download latest invoice only fetch the newest one? Where are the older ones kept?

expect.reference: Yes, it downloads only the most recent invoice. Older ones are not on the page: they are in the emails sent each month, and support can send a copy of any invoice from the last 12 months.

cases.question: do you keep the full card number on file anywhere

expect.reference: No, Acme does not store full card numbers; its payment provider holds them. The page shows only the type of card and its last four digits.

cases.question: which card brands can a workspace pay with?

expect.reference: Three are accepted: Visa, Mastercard and American Express.

cases.question: whats the round A in the top right for

expect.reference: It opens a menu with three choices: Settings, Plan and billing, and Sign out. Everything about the account, such as settings, plan, payment and security, is reached from it.

cases.question: If I sign out here, am I signed out on my other laptop too?

expect.reference: No, signing out only ends the session in the browser you are using. You stay signed in on any other browser.

cases.question: supported browsers?

expect.reference: It works in the current versions of four browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge.

cases.question: How fast does support usually get back to people?

expect.reference: Within one business day. A workspace on the Business plan gets its first reply within 4 working hours.

cases.question: I got an email that says it's from Acme support and it wants one of my two-factor codes. Is that something your support team would ever ask for?

expect.reference: No, support never asks for a password, an API key's secret value, a two-factor code or a full card number. Do not answer the message; forward it to support instead.

cases.question: is support open on weekends

expect.reference: No, support works Monday to Friday only, from 09:00 to 18:00 UTC. It is also closed on 25 December and 1 January.

cases.question: We've got two-factor switched on for everyone here and I'm about to invite a contractor. How long does she have to accept, and what will she need to do the first time she logs in?

expect.reference: The link in the invite email works for 7 days. Because the requirement is on, she sets up two-factor authentication the first time she signs in, using an authenticator app that gives 6-digit codes.

cases.question: we ran out of requests for the month. can we still push a fix live, and when do our projects start taking traffic again

expect.reference: Yes, deploys are not counted as requests, so a fix can still be deployed after the limit is reached. Requests are refused with a 429 response until the count resets at midnight UTC on the 1st of the month, or until the workspace moves to a larger plan.

cases.question: One of our developers is leaving, and the build server deploys with the API key he's been using. If the owner takes him off the team, will deploys break? And what happens to the projects he set up?

expect.reference: Deploys keep working, because an API key belongs to the workspace and not to a person, and it goes on working after the person who used it leaves. The projects he created, and everything he deployed, stay in the workspace and keep running.

cases.question: our project is in US East but nearly all our users are in europe. can we swtich it to EU West? and if it has to be a new project over there, how do we get our code onto it

expect.reference: No, a project's region cannot be changed once the project exists. Create a second project with EU West as its region and deploy the app to it with the Acme command line tool and an API key; the original project carries on running.

cases.question: team plan seat limit? and do invites that haven't been accepted yet use up a seat

expect.reference: The Team plan allows 10 people, and the owner counts as one of them. An invite that has not been accepted does not count towards that number; a person counts only once they accept and join.

cases.question: Someone the owner took off the workspace back in the spring is coming back to work with us. Can she be added again, and how long will she have to accept?

expect.reference: Yes, someone who was removed can be invited again; she needs a new invite and comes back as a member. The link in that invite works for 7 days.

cases.question: if the owner makes 2fa mandatory, does the api key our CI uses stop working? and does everybody get logged out right then

expect.reference: No to both. API keys are not affected by the two-factor requirement, and nobody is signed out when it is turned on: each person is asked to set it up at their next sign-in.

cases.question: Do the deploy emails also go out when a deploy fails? And can the time in them be shown in Pacific time instead?

expect.reference: Yes, the workspace owner is emailed about every deploy, failed ones included. The time in those emails follows the workspace time zone, which the owner can set to Pacific on the General tab of Settings.

cases.question: Can ordinary members see the request count too, or only the owner? And how often is that number refreshed?

expect.reference: Members can see it as well: the workspace's usage is in the Usage this month card on the Overview page. The figure is refreshed about every 10 minutes.

cases.question: A colleague dropped her phone in a lake and her authenticator app was on it. Is there any other way for her to sign in? And if support has to get involved, how quickly do they answer?

expect.reference: She can sign in with one of her backup codes; if none are left, the workspace owner writes to support to have her two-factor setup reset. Support replies within one business day, or within 4 working hours for a workspace on the Business plan.

cases.question: we think one of our api keys leaked.. can it be shut off from this page? and what would support need from us to help

expect.reference: No, Acme Console has no way to switch a key off; the workspace owner writes to support, who do it. The message must come from the owner's email address and should give the workspace name, what happened and when.

cases.question: Typo in a project name. Can it be renamed, and if not, can support do it?

expect.reference: No. A project's name is part of its web address, so it cannot be changed after the project is created, and support cannot change it either.

cases.question: what name do people see in the invite email, and can they accept with a different address than the one it was sent to

expect.reference: The invite email shows the workspace name. The person has to accept with the same email address the invite went to.

cases.question: I can't find a button to start a deploy anywhere. Is there one? Also, once an API key is created, where do we see its secret?

expect.reference: Acme Console has no button for deploying: deploys are started with the Acme command line tool, using one of the workspace's API keys. A key's secret is never shown in the list; it is sent once to the workspace owner's email address, as a link that opens one time within 24 hours.

cases.question: what if it runs out before they get round to it

history.text: how long is an invite link good for?
The link in the invite email works for 7 days.

expect.reference: Send the invite again: enter the same address and press Send invite. That gives a fresh link good for another 7 days and cancels the old one.

cases.question: and who's allowed to take them off again?

history.text: Can anyone here invite people, or just the owner?
Anyone in the workspace can invite a new teammate. All it takes is the person's email address.

expect.reference: Only the owner of the workspace can remove someone; a member cannot.

cases.question: Does anyone get notifed about it?

history.text: What happens if a deploy fails?
Nothing changes: the previous version stays live, and the command line tool prints the reason.

expect.reference: Yes. The workspace owner is emailed about every deploy, failed ones included, with the project, the result and the time.

cases.question: do those ever expire?

history.text: what do we need to deploy from our build server
Deploys are started with the Acme command line tool, using one of the workspace's API keys.

expect.reference: No, API keys never expire.

cases.question: can they get them by text instead

history.text: what kind of app do people need for the two-factor codes?
Any authenticator app that produces 6-digit codes will work.

expect.reference: No, getting the codes by text message is not supported.

cases.question: Do the ones we don't use roll over to next month?

history.text: What exactly counts as a request?
A request is one call received by any of your deployed projects. It counts whether the project answers successfully or with an error.

expect.reference: No. Unused requests are not carried into the next month; the count goes back to zero on the 1st.

cases.question: Would that break our project URLs or API keys?

history.text: Who's allowed to rename the workspace?
Only the workspace owner, in Workspace name on the General tab of Settings.

expect.reference: No. Renaming the workspace leaves the projects, their web addresses, the API keys and the teammates as they are.

cases.question: and if I end it early on this one, does that end it on the others too?

history.text: how long does a login last here
